1.title: Modern Network Environments
1.text: Welcome to Module seven: Modern Network Environments. It covers the exam area one point zero Networking Concepts. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do seven things. one point eight Summarize evolving use cases for modern network environments: software-defined network (S D N) and S D-W A N. Virtual Extensible L A N (V X L A N). Zero trust architecture (Z T A). Secure Access Service Edge (S A S E) and Security Service Edge (S S E). Infrastructure as code. IPv six addressing. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: one point zero Networking Concepts (twenty-three percent). Exam format: up to ninety questions in ninety minutes; a score of seven hundred twenty on a scale of one hundred to nine hundred passes. Validated against: the official Comp T I A Network plus N ten to nine exam objectives, version four point zero.

1.title: SDN and SD-WAN
1.text: S D N and S D-W A N. Software-defined networking (S D N) separates the control plane (decisions) from the data plane (forwarding) and centralizes control in a controller that devices follow. S D-W A N applies S D N ideas to the wide area network. Application aware. Chooses a path by application (voice over the best link). Zero-touch provisioning. A new device configures itself from the central controller on power-up. Transport agnostic. Works over any link: M P L S, broadband, cellular. Central policy management. One place defines policy for all sites.

1.title: SDN and SD-WAN, continued
1.text: S D N and S D-W A N. The figure shows this: An S D-W A N controller managing sites over several transports.

1.title: VXLAN
1.text: V X L A N. Virtual Extensible L A N (V X L A N) encapsulates layer two frames inside U D P or I P so a layer two network can span a layer three network. It uses a twenty-four-bit V X L A N network identifier (about sixteen million segments) instead of the V L A N limit of four thousand ninety-four.

1.title: VXLAN, continued
1.text: V X L A N. Data center interconnect (D C I). Extends the same layer two segment between data centers. Layer two encapsulation. M A C frames carried in I P packets.

1.title: Zero trust and SASE
1.text: Zero trust and S A S E. Zero trust architecture (Z T A). Never trust, always verify: no implicit trust from network location. Policy-based authentication. Every request is checked against policy (user, device, context). Authorization or least privilege access. Grant only the access needed, for the shortest time. S A S E (Secure Access Service Edge). Cloud service combining networking (S D-W A N) and security (firewall, secure web gateway, zero trust access). S S E (Security Service Edge). The security half of S A S E (without the networking). Exam tip: "No device is trusted just because it is inside the network" equals zero trust. S A S E equals S D-W A N plus cloud-delivered security; S S E equals only the security part.

1.title: Infrastructure as code (IaC)
1.text: Infrastructure as code. I A C manages network configuration through code instead of manual changes. Automation. Playbooks, templates and reusable tasks apply the same configuration everywhere. Configuration drift. Devices change away from the intended configuration; I A C detects and corrects it (compliance). Upgrades. Rolled out by script consistently. Dynamic inventories. The device list is built automatically from the environment. Source control. Version control, a central repository, conflict identification, branching.

1.title: IPv6
1.text: IPv six. Size. one hundred twenty-eight bits, written in hexadecimal groups, for example two thousand one db eight one; replaces one run of zeros. Why. Mitigates IPv four address exhaustion. Compatibility. Dual stack (run IPv four and IPv six together), tunneling (carry IPv six inside IPv four), N A T sixty-four (lets IPv six-only hosts reach IPv four services). Addresses. No broadcast; link-local fe eighty slash ten; loopback one. Exam tip: S D-W A N is the W A N version of S D N; V X L A N stretches layer two over layer three; S A S E adds security to S D-W A N. Exam tip: IPv six transition tools: dual stack (both), tunneling (IPv six inside IPv four), N A T sixty-four (IPv six-only to IPv four).

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A retailer wants new branch routers to configure themselves when plugged in, using central policy. Which technology fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: S D-W A N with zero-touch provisioning. S D-W A N controllers provision devices automatically.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A company wants to extend a layer two segment across two data centers over an I P network. Which technology fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: V X L A N. V X L A N carries layer two frames over layer three.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A policy states that every access request is verified regardless of network location. Which model is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Zero trust architecture. Zero trust never assumes trust from location.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Network devices slowly drift from the approved configuration after manual changes. What helps most? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Infrastructure as code with compliance checks. I A C detects and corrects configuration drift.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Which technology lets IPv six-only clients reach IPv four-only servers? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: N A T sixty-four. N A T sixty-four translates between IPv six and IPv four.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which service combines S D-W A N with cloud-delivered security? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: S A S E. S A S E combines networking and security; S S E is only the security part.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What does S D N separate? Answer: The control plane from the data plane. Question two. How many bits is an IPv six address? Answer: one hundred twenty-eight. Question three. What does V X L A N encapsulate? Answer: Layer two frames, inside U D P or I P.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What is configuration drift? Answer: Devices changing away from the intended configuration. Question five. What does dual stack mean? Answer: Running IPv four and IPv six together. Question six. What does least privilege mean? Answer: Granting only the access that is needed.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. S D N or S D-W A N: central controller; application aware, zero-touch, transport agnostic, central policy. V X L A N: layer two over layer three; D C I; twenty-four-bit identifier. Zero trust or S A S E: never trust, always verify; S A S E equals S D-W A N plus security; S S E equals security. I A C: playbooks and templates, drift, dynamic inventories, source control. IPv six: one hundred twenty-eight bits; dual stack, tunneling, N A T sixty-four.
